1.why: Clean sans-serif typeface is used throughout with adequate letter and line spacing on the white cards.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case without italics or all-caps, and text is broken into short paragraphs rather than dense blocks.

3.why: Layouts are single-column cards with large inputs and buttons that remain readable and well spaced at mobile width.

4.why: Most instructions are brief plain-language sentences such as 'Enter the six-digit verification code' or 'Keep the setup key private.'

5.why: No example format is shown for expected inputs such as the verification code, authenticator code, or recovery-code pattern.

6.why: Progress never depends on reading a long block; each screen has only a short title, one-line description, and brief callouts.

7.why: Setup key and recovery codes appear as selectable text that can be copied, yet no explicit copy button is provided and codes must still be typed into authenticator/confirmation fields.

8.why: Copy mentions scanning a setup key but no QR code or equivalent visual alternative is actually displayed on the add-authenticator screens.

9.why: Standard email/password inputs should allow browser autofill and password managers, but no autocomplete attributes or explicit support are visible.

10.why: Large page titles and prominent blue primary buttons make the current step and main action stand out clearly on every screen.

11.why: Each screen requests only one primary action (Continue, Verify identity, Confirm authenticator, Save codes, etc.).

12.why: After actions the UI states outcomes plainly, e.g. 'MFA is active', 'Recovery code confirmed', and 'That recovery code has been used and cannot be used again.'

13.why: Users can re-request or generate new recovery codes, navigate back to MFA status, and retry entry without apparent lockout or penalty.

14.why: The only observed error ('We could not complete that request. Please try again.') states no specific problem and gives no fix guidance.

15.why: No countdown timers or expiration warnings appear on any code-entry or reading screen, implying generous time.
